headline: power has doubled in a year, and the coming winter led this week's rise
commentary: UK power spot is 162.50 £/MWh, up 7.1% since our update on 7 October and now double where it was a year ago, the highest level in the three years shown here. The gas front month, November, is 206.75 p/therm, up 9.0% since 7 October. That takes it back above where it stood before the late-September fall and within half a percent of September's peak. Several things are pushing at once: an Iranian strike on an LPG carrier and warnings to shipping across the wider Middle East, with no sign of de-escalation; a colder forecast for late this week and next; weak wind and solar across Europe; French nuclear output held back by low rivers; and the plan to link UK and EU carbon markets, which has lifted UK carbon prices to eight-month highs. Unlike last time, the rise landed on this winter. November to March are up about 8 to 9%, Summer 27 4.4% and Summer 28 1.4%. That widens the gap between this winter and next year, which strengthens the case for term. A 12-month contract starting in November is about 0.79 p/kWh higher on a wholesale-equivalent basis than on 7 October, a 24-month around 0.5 p/kWh, and the 24-month now sits around 17% below the 12-month, up from 16%. Weather and shipping risk can ease quickly; carbon linking will not, and waiting has now cost money in both updates since late September. Day-ahead prices this past week ran from £9.28/MWh early on Saturday to £162.18 on Monday morning, the swing a fixed price removes.

gas.note: NBP front month Nov 26 is 206.75 p/therm, up 9.0% on its 7 Oct print of 189.74 and above its 18 Sep level of 199.45, so the late-September fall has fully reversed. The rest of this winter: Dec 26 209.20, Jan 27 210.37, Feb 27 208.25, Mar 27 197.99, Q1 27 205.30. This time the rise is led by the front of the curve: the winter months are up 7.8 to 9.0%, against Summer 27 150.92 (+4.4%) and Summer 28 90.25 (+1.4%). So the step-down from this winter has widened: Q1 27 205.30 to Summer 27 150.92 is a 26.5% discount, from 23.6% on 7 Oct, and Summer 28 at 90.25 is a further step below. A 24-month contract blends this winter down with cheaper 2027 and 2028, and that blend did more work this week than last.
